subject: error building derivatives with dynamic indexing

messages.author: 7fe97f8ba9e0dcfe
messages.subject: error building derivatives with dynamic indexing
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to create a model with AD, and I am getting type errors when compiling my model. I think I have tracked the error to be related to dynamic indexing of arguments of my nimblefunctions.

For example, these lines are part of my model code:
for(i in 1:nsite){
    for(t in 2:totalt[i]){
     
        pic_trap[t-1,1:totalo[t,i],i,1:nsize] <- calc_cond_prob(totalo[t,i],nsize,
                                                              hazard[t-1,1:totalo[t,i],i,1:nsize])
}}

And then the  calc_cond_prob function looks like this:

calc_cond_prob <- nimbleFunction(
  #input and output types
  run = function(nobs = double(0), 
                 nsize = double(0), 
                 hazard = double(2)) 
  {
    returnType(double(2))  
   
    # create empty array
    array <- nimArray(dim = c(nobs, nsize))

    #loop through sizes
    for(k in 1:nsize){
      array[1:nobs,k] <- hazard[1:nobs,k] / sum(hazard[1:nobs,k])
    }
    return(array)
  },
  buildDerivs = list(run = list(ignore = c('k','nobs','nsize')))
)

If I pretend that totalo[t,i] is static and replace it with nobs (where I define nobs as a constant), I no longer get compilation errors:

for(i in 1:nsite){
    for(t in 2:totalt[i]){
     
        pic_trap[t-1,1:nobs,i,1:nsize] <- calc_cond_prob(nobs,nsize,
                                                              hazard[t-1,1:nobs,i,1:nsize])
}}

This indexing of totalo[t,i] as the nobs argument is found in multiple nimblefunctions in my model code.

Do you have any suggestions for how to deal with this? I'm thinking I should be casting the type of nobs within my nimble functions?

Please let me know if there is more detail I can provide!
Thanks,
Abby Keller

messages.subject: Re: error building derivatives with dynamic indexing
parts: I followed up with Perry off-list, and creating the following non-derivative tracked integers (nobs_int and nsize_int) worked for me in my nimbleFunction. The model now compiles!:

run = function(nobs = double(0), # scalar
                 nsize = double(0), #scalar
                 hazard = double(2)) # 2-d array
  {
    returnType(double(2))  # 2-d array return
   
    nobs_int <- ADbreak(nobs)
    nsize_int <- ADbreak(nsize)
   
    # Conditional multinomial cell probabilities
    #create empty array
    array <- nimArray(dim = c(nobs_int, nsize_int))
    #loop through sizes
    for(k in 1:nsize_int){
      #P(capture in trap j | captured at all)
      array[1:nobs_int,k] <- hazard[1:nobs_int,k] / sum(hazard[1:nobs_int,k])
    }
    return(array)
  },
  buildDerivs = list(run = list(ignore = c('k','nobs_int','nsize_int')))
)
